evidence.quote: I would say that an expectation of higher near-term policy rates does not appear to be causing the increase in longer-term rates.
could become further strained if corporate earnings fall due to a sharper-than-expected slowdown in economic activity.
In China, a further slowdown in economic growth could worsen financial stresses.
Internationally, inflationary pressures persist in advanced foreign economies and could pose risks to the global financial system.
In my view, our financial system is substantially more resilient than it was in the mid-2000s

parsed.rationale: This is a financial stability speech with little direct monetary policy signal; it mostly emphasizes downside risks (CRE, China, geopolitics) and mentions inflation pressures only as a global risk. The remark that higher long yields do not reflect expectations of higher policy rates is mildly dovish, so net stance is near neutral with a slight dovish tilt.
